name: ERC-8004 vs Google A2A Governance Dataset, Croissant Release
description: Versioned machine-readable release of the RQ1 governance dataset. It separates the R1 annotation archive, R2 cross-model consensus, and R2 cross-round consensus.
citeAs: kl41r3 (2026). ERC-8004 vs Google A2A Governance Dataset, Croissant release 1.0.1.
dataCollection: Public Ethereum Magicians and GitHub governance records, followed by LLM annotation and model-consensus construction.
rai:dataLimitations: This dataset is restricted to public Ethereum Magicians and GitHub traces from two AI protocol ecosystems and therefore does not represent private meetings, internal corporate coordination, all blockchain communities, or governance outcomes in general. It is not recommended for causal claims about governance form, profiling individuals, or training systems that make consequential decisions about contributors.
rai:dataBiases: Public-platform traces omit private corporate coordination and may overrepresent highly active, English-speaking, technically experienced contributors. Selection bias arises from platform and retention filters, and institutional labels have lower inter-model agreement than several other annotation fields.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Contains public handles, display names, authored text, timestamps, public profile information, and inferred or documented institutional-affiliation labels. It does not intentionally collect private contact information, health data, financial data, or government identifiers. Public identifiers may nevertheless enable reidentification.
rai:dataUseCases: Validated uses include reproducible analysis of observable participation, discourse composition, annotation reliability, and network structure in the ERC and A2A public records represented here. The dataset may support methods research on computational governance analysis. Validity has not been established for causal inference, population estimation, individual evaluation, automated moderation, or model training for decisions that affect contributors.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Potential benefits include more transparent study of technology standardization, reproducible governance research, and evidence for more accountable participation procedures. Risks include decontextualizing public comments, amplifying noisy affiliation labels, or using activity measures to rank individuals. Mitigations include public-source provenance, explicit uncertainty and scope statements, checksum manifests, a non-commercial license, and a stated prohibition on consequential person-level use.
